q: What has area, height, mass and more than one surface?
n: Form is three-dimensional, with area, height, mass and several surfaces. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the feel of a surface that can evoke emotion?
n: Texture is the feel of a surface, which can evoke emotion. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: The Salk Institute in La Jolla, California, where there is a balance of the buildings on either side, is a great example of which ordering principle of architecture?
n: The Salk Institute's two building rows mirror each other across a central plaza and water channel, a classic example of symmetry. Source: Salk Institute (architecture); Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which attribute of color is its purity, intensity or saturation?
n: Chroma is the purity, intensity or saturation of a colour. High-chroma colours are vivid. Low-chroma colours are grayed or muted. Source: Munsell Color System.

q: What is the identifying character of a volume, set by the shapes and relations of its planes?
n: Form is the identifying character of a volume, set by the shapes and relations of its planes. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which symmetry lets a composition be split into similar halves by a plane at any angle through a central axis?
n: Radial symmetry lets a composition be divided into similar halves by a plane at any angle through a central axis. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Which principle shows the relative importance and roles of forms and spaces in an organization?
n: Hierarchy, an ordering principle, shows the relative importance and roles of forms and spaces in an organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What movement comes from patterned repetition or alternation of elements?
n: Rhythm is movement created by patterned repetition or alternation of elements. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is exact correspondence of size, form and arrangement on opposite sides of a dividing line?
n: Symmetry is exact correspondence of size, form and arrangement on opposite sides of a dividing line or plane. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the act of repeating elements or motifs in a design?
n: Repetition is repeating elements or motifs in a design. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is prominence given to an element through contrast, anomaly or counterpoint?
n: Emphasis gives an element prominence through contrast, anomaly or counterpoint. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is a system of elements ranked by importance?
n: A hierarchy is a system of elements ranked by importance. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the quality of being identical, homogeneous or regular?
n: Uniformity is the quality of being identical, homogeneous or regular. Source: Merriam-Webster; Ching.

q: Changing material, color and texture across a surface is:
n: Changing material, colour and texture across a surface is surface articulation. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Applying color to an object's surface is:
n: Applying colour to a surface changes how it reads, which is surface articulation. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: When the edge of a cube is chamfered, what is being done?
n: Chamfering a cube's edge changes how its planes meet, which is articulation of form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: There is a colonnade that consists of identical columns. What type of system arrangement is this?
n: A colonnade of identical columns in a row is a linear arrangement of repeated elements. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What way of joining makes the parts clear and distinct from one another?
n: Articulation joins parts so they stay clear and distinct from one another. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What describes shapes whose value depends only on their own lines, colors and relations?
n: Abstract shapes have value only through their own lines, colours and relations, with no reference to real objects. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order; Encyclopaedia Britannica, abstract art.

q: What form results from removing a portion without losing the sense of the whole?
n: A subtractive form results from removing a portion of a volume while keeping the sense of the whole. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the manner of arranging and coordinating the parts of a composition to produce a coherent image?
n: Organization is arranging and coordinating the parts of a composition to produce a coherent image. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the structure of a surface from the size, shape and arrangement of its parts?
n: Texture is the structure of a surface, from the size, shape and arrangement of its parts. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is arranging parts in proper relation to form a unified whole?
n: Composition is arranging parts in proper relation to form a unified whole. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is systematically arranging interdependent parts into a coherent whole?
n: Organization is systematically arranging interdependent parts into a coherent whole. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the guiding concept that starts an architectural design?
n: The parti (parti pris) is the guiding concept that starts an architectural design. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is a repeated decorative motif that gives a surface rhythm and continuity?
n: A pattern is a repeated decorative motif that gives a surface rhythm and continuity. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is the spatial organization of figure A?
n: Figure A groups spaces around one dominant central space, a centralized organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the spatial organization of figure B?
n: Figure B is a sequence of spaces along a line, a linear organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the spatial organization of figure C?
n: Figure C has linear arms radiating from a central space, a radial organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the spatial organization of figure D?
n: Figure D groups spaces by proximity and shared traits, a clustered organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the spatial organization of figure E?
n: Figure E sets spaces on a regular three-dimensional grid, a grid organization. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the art movement behind the celebration of industrial materials and the elimination of ornament in favor of a sleek, machinelike aesthetic in architecture?
n: The International Style celebrated industrial materials and eliminated ornament for a sleek, machine-like aesthetic. Source: Hitchcock & Johnson, The International Style (1932); Encyclopaedia Britannica.
